title: The paper rocket
summary: Dani builds a paper rocket and flies all the way to a yellow star.

scenes.text:
Dani was five years old and had a dream so big it almost didn't fit in his chest: he wanted to travel to space. In his bedroom, the walls were covered with maps of planets that he had taped up himself, with his tongue sticking out from concentration.

Big Jupiter, Saturn with his ring, red little Mars, blue Earth like a marble. On his bed, his favorite stuffed animal, an astronaut named Pepe, watched him always with the same painted smile. One soft, windy afternoon, after eating his snack, Dani took a clean white sheet from his notebook.

He smoothed it out on his desk and began to fold it very, very carefully. Fold up, fold in the middle, fold the corners, fold of the fold. His little fingers worked slowly, without rushing, biting his lip in concentration.

The sheet of paper transformed: first it looked like a little boat, then a hat, then... a rocket! He held it in his hands, white and shining like the full moon.

Dani looked at it with pride, smiled, and whispered softly: "Ready to take off, friend?"

Dani opened his bedroom window and leaned out to the night sky. His hair was ruffled by the breeze. The night air smelled of closed flowers.

The stars twinkled up there like curious little eyes, waiting for something. Dani lifted the paper rocket with both hands, pointed it at the sky and started the countdown in a low voice. "Three...

two... one..." And he threw it into the air with all his strength.

Whoosh!

The rocket went up and up, faster and faster, leaving a trail of silver sparkles behind. It passed the tops of the trees, passed the neighbor's balcony with the cats, passed the sleeping white clouds. It left behind the little birds resting in their nests and the bats playing among the branches.

And then, without knowing how — because magic things always happen like that, without warning — Dani found himself on top of the rocket, holding the tip with his little hands, eyes wide as two plates, cheeks rosy. He was actually flying!

Up there, far beyond the clouds, a chubby yellow star was waiting for him. She had the face of a kind grandmother, with round cheeks, a huge smile, and rays that came out of her like locks of golden hair. "Hello Dani, I was waiting for you," the star said with a singing voice, as if she had known him forever.

Dani went silent for a moment, then lowered his gaze, shy. The star reached out a ray as if it were a hand. "Would you like to dance with me among the constellations?"

Dani took her hand of light without hesitating. They started dancing together, slowly at first, then faster. They flew between comets with fiery tails and greeted the moon.

They played hide and seek with three tiny planets and tickled Saturn on his ring until he shook all over with laughter.

The Milky Way was like a river of glowing milk, and Dani and the star crossed it hand in hand. "This is the most beautiful thing I've ever seen," whispered Dani. The star answered: "And the best part is yet to come."

The star showed Dani a tiny box of light she kept among her rays. She opened it slowly, and out came thousands of golden sparkles that scattered across the sky forming pictures: a boat, a dog, a smile. Dani had never seen so much magic.

"These are dream seeds," the star explained. "Every night I plant some so that the children who look up at the sky will want to imagine." Dani helped her plant several, blowing them with his puffed-up cheeks until they flew far away.

Suddenly, he felt a little sleepy, his eyes heavy. The star noticed and blew him a warm caress. When Dani opened his eyes, he was already back in his bed, snug under the covers.

The paper rocket was on his nightstand, right where he had left it. Through the window, the yellow star winked at him from far away, as if to say "until tomorrow." Dani smiled and hugged Pepe his stuffed animal tightly.

That night he learned an important secret he would remember all his life: imagining is also flying. And any child with a sheet of paper can reach the stars.
